sections.title: Noun suffixes
sections.content:
Suffixes that turn words into nouns:
• -ment: achieve → achievement, develop → development. This is a remarkable achievement.
• -tion/-sion: educate → education, decide → decision. Education opens doors to opportunity.
• -ness: happy → happiness, aware → awareness. Awareness of the issue is growing.
• -ity: creative → creativity, electric → electricity. Creativity is valued in every profession.
• -er/-or: teach → teacher, invent → inventor. The inventor was awarded a patent.

sections.title: Adjective and verb suffixes
sections.content:
Suffixes for forming adjectives and verbs:
• -able/-ible: enjoy → enjoyable, access → accessible. The museum is fully accessible to wheelchair users.
• -ful: care → careful, hope → hopeful. She remains hopeful about the future.
• -less: care → careless, hope → hopeless. The situation seemed completely hopeless.
• -ise/-ize: modern → modernise, real → realise. They plan to modernise the entire building.
• -ous: danger → dangerous, fame → famous. Swimming in the river can be dangerous.

exercises.question: What is the noun form of 'achieve'?
Which suffix means 'without'?
exercises.explanation: The suffix -less means without (e.g., careless = without care).

exercises.question: The adjective form of 'enjoy' is:
exercises.explanation: Enjoyable is formed with the suffix -able, meaning 'able to be enjoyed'.

exercises.question: Which suffix turns a verb into 'a person who does something'?
exercises.explanation: The suffix -er creates nouns meaning 'a person who does' (teacher, writer).

exercises.question: Adding -ise/-ize to 'modern' creates:
exercises.explanation: Modernise is a verb formed with -ise, meaning 'to make modern'.

exercises.question: The suffix '-ous' creates which type of word?
